correctness.rationale: Reparameterizing by \(\delta=1/\gamma\) cancels all parameter powers in the source likelihood and yields an exact log-derivative. The elementary inequality \(y/(1+\delta y)\ge y/(1+\delta)\) proves global boundary monotonicity when the weighted-time statistic is at least the failure count. When the statistic is smaller, the derivative is positive at the boundary, negative asymptotically, and the likelihood tends to zero, proving existence of a finite global maximizer. The checker independently verifies both parameterizations and representative interior/boundary cases.

value.rationale: Maximum likelihood is one of the paper's two central inferential frameworks, and its simulations, bootstrap procedures, Wald intervals, and real-data comparisons rely on finite numerical estimates. The theorem gives an exact data-level gate that distinguishes samples with a genuine finite MLE from samples whose likelihood is maximized only at the uniform boundary. The failure region has positive probability under the model, so this is not a merely formal endpoint check. The criterion can be applied before Newton-Raphson and prevents interpreting divergent or very large iterates as ordinary finite estimates.
